title: Kami UI
description: Architecting a high-performance, design-token-first component library for hyper-growth fintech platforms. Solving the friction between radical brand expression and accessibility standards.

seo.title: Kami UI — Case Study
seo.description: How a token-first component library replaced CSS override sprawl with a single source of design truth.

items.src: Existing UI kits prioritized generic 'SaaS' aesthetics over the brutalist, high-contrast identity required by the Kami brand. This led to "Shadow CSS" sprawl where engineers were constantly overriding library defaults.

src: 84% of components had custom CSS overrides.
Accessibility scores averaged below 70 due to radical typography.
Design-to-Dev handoff took 3x longer than industry benchmark.

items.alt: A brutalist wireframe mesh diagram representing the fragmented component architecture before the rebuild.

items.src: We abandoned the traditional 'component-first' mentality. Instead, we built a Rust-based engine that generates CSS variables from a single JSON source of truth, ensuring every pixel—from border-radius to motion curves—is governed by the core architecture schema.

src.title: Flexibility vs. Integrity
src.desc: We chose to hard-lock layouts into a 12-column Swiss grid. This reduced developer freedom but eliminated 100% of "off-grid" design drifts across four separate product teams.

src.title: Static vs. Dynamic
src.desc: Opted for pre-compiled CSS-in-Rust over runtime CSS-in-JS. Increased build times by 12s, but reduced interaction latency by 45ms—critical for high-frequency trading dashboards.

items.src: The brand demanded editorial typography (120px display text) that needed to remain responsive across mobile viewports without losing its 'expensive' feel. Standard Tailwind utilities failed at these extremes.
Maintaining the 'Burnt Orange' accent's vibrancy on a #141313 background while passing WCAG AA standards was nearly impossible with traditional hex mapping.
The most valuable architecture is the one that says "no" for you.

By building strict structural lines and uncompromising grids into the framework, we shifted the engineering culture from "how do I style this?" to "how do I structure this?". The UI became a byproduct of solid architecture, rather than a decorative layer.
